baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Challenges a specific Marxist/Jacobin historiography of the French Revolution for reproducing revolutionary and commemorative categories.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Primary pp. 255–256 read. Furet’s polemical label and diagnosis remain his claims about a specific historiographical dispute, not a critique of every Marxist or a personal arrow to Marx.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Examines political language and claims to represent the people as mechanisms of revolutionary power.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Named reader Gérard Grunberg, pp. 895 and 897, on Penser. Full book unread; no universal acceptance, deterministic twentieth-century analogy or inference from institutional membership.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Ginzburg disputes Furet’s restriction of subordinate-class history to quantitative and anonymous reconstruction, defending individual cases where the evidence permits.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: He explicitly names Furet before defending the possibility of reconstructing individual personalities. This is a methodological criticism, not rejection of quantitative history as such or proof of every Menocchio interpretation. Furet’s underlying text was not newly read.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Corbin criticizes the republic-centered account he associates with Furet for reducing much of nineteenth-century France to steps toward a later republican outcome.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Own 2006 answer also names Maurice Agulhon, whose credit is retained here without inventing a standalone endpoint. Corbin argues for studying monarchies, conflicting political emotions and other periods on their own terms. This records his specific historiographical criticism, not a claim that all of Furet’s work is teleological; Furet’s original books remain unread in this dossier.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Roche recalls contributing his study of booksellers’ classifications to Furet’s book-history inquiry and receiving Furet’s acknowledgment for it.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Own retrospective answer15, printed164, specifically identifies Livre et Société and note16 in Furet’s text. The original Furet acknowledgment was not independently read here. This is a recalled research contribution, not an inference from knowing Furet or sole authorship of the inquiry.
